Thanks Laura — excellent questions. Answering inline and looping in Dev for the detailed technical boundary language: 

1) Isolation guarantees (high level):
- Hosted API: multi-tenant inference pool. We provide strong logical isolation (per-request auth, request-level logging tied to customer id), but the runtime shares compute & KV caching across tenants by default for efficiency. Because of shared caching and telemetry, we treat Hosted API as "not eligible" for PHI by default unless a customer purchases a Dedicated or Private instance with explicit isolation controls.
- Dedicated: customer-dedicated GPU pools and isolated tenant VMs/containers. KV cache and model-serving nodes are reserved for the customer; telemetry is segregated by tenant id. This mode is eligible for PHI processing when a BAA is in place and customer's network/VPC controls are configured.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full control plane isolation. We offer both a VPC-hosted private deployment (managed by Redwood in your cloud account) and an on-prem installation package for air-gapped environments. Both Private options are eligible for PHI with a signed BAA.

2) Shared layers: the main shared components in Hosted are telemetry/metrics pipelines and optional cross-customer prefix caching. We can disable cross-customer caching for Dedicated/Private and provide additional logs that show per-request scoping.

3) SOC 2 scope: Our SOC 2 Type II covers the Redwood inference platform and control plane services used by Dedicated and Hosted offerings. For Private on-prem deployments, certain infrastructure controls are out of scope (customer-managed infra), but we provide an addendum and guidance for the controls customers must implement. Dev — can you confirm exact SOC 2 wording we should provide to Laura and attach the attestation PDF?

Procurement note: Dedicated has reserved-capacity pricing and typically involves a 6–12 month commit for committed discounting; we can be flexible at proof-of-concept stage.

Next step: Laura, if your security team can complete the questionnaire, we’ll review and return answers + a draft BAA for your legal team.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Laura / Marissa —

Following up with the technical boundary language you can pass to your security team and legal:

- PHI handling boundary: Redwood will process PHI only within customer-dedicated or private deployment environments. For Dedicated, the GPU pool, serving nodes, and KV cache are reserved to the customer; we will disable cross-tenant KV/prefix caching and provide per-request metadata to show PHI scoping. For Private on-prem, all data remains in your VPC or air-gapped environment as configured by your infra team.
- Telemetry & logs: Application-level logs and telemetry that include request metadata are segregated by tenant. PII/PHI is redacted from centralized analytics; we provide options for customers to ship logs to their own logging endpoint (recommended for PHI workloads).
- Encryption: Data in transit is TLS 1.2+; data at rest in dedicated/private deployments is encrypted with customer-managed KMS where requested.
- BAA: Redwood legal will prepare a standard BAA; typical turnaround is 3–5 business days from receipt of legal redlines. We will not enable PHI processing until a mutually executed BAA is in place.

If you want, I can also (a) provide the SOC 2 attestation PDF and (b) fill out the Excel questionnaire line-by-line and return with highlighted answers.

- Marissa: I’ll prepare the SOC 2 attestation and a draft BAA template you can share with MedAssist legal.
